incidents.vector: Operators posing as Americans used ChatGPT to mass-produce images and social posts amplifying anger over AI data centers and US tariffs, spread via VPN-masked fake X and YouTube accounts.
incidents.impact: OpenAI disrupted two likely China-origin influence clusters; campaigns gained little organic traction (rated 1-2 on the breakout scale) but show AI being used to inflame existing US domestic divisions.

incidents.vector: Russian operators hijacked existing Bluesky accounts since April to post pro-Kremlin, anti-Ukraine propaganda produced by the Matryoshka disinformation network.
incidents.impact: Bluesky has been suspending compromised accounts until owners can resecure them; part of a sustained Russian narrative-control effort tied to the war in Ukraine.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted the territorial government's email servers; officials have not specified whether ransomware was involved.
incidents.impact: Email outages are expected to slow administrative operations for the US territory's government.

incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators (FIOD) arrested the operators of MIRhosting/WorkTitans for providing infrastructure to EU-sanctioned, Russia-linked hosting used in DDoS, influence and disinformation operations.
incidents.impact: Over 800 servers were seized — including infrastructure tied to pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies during November 2025 municipal elections — and customer data on those servers was lost.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS / GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor is actively exploiting CVE-2026-0257, an authentication-bypass flaw in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway components, to initiate unauthorized VPN sessions.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed in-the-wild exploitation (CVE added to CISA KEV on May 29); a small portion of probed devices established VPN sessions, though no post-access lateral movement has been observed yet.

incidents.vector: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-20245, an input-validation flaw in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager allowing authenticated/local attackers to run commands as root, often chained with earlier Cisco zero-days (CVE-2026-20182/20127) to gain the required access.
incidents.impact: Seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year; no patch or workaround is available, and Cisco observed limited cases of malicious configuration changes pushed to edge devices.

incidents.vector: CVE-2026-41091, an elevation-of-privilege flaw in Microsoft Defender, lets an attacker with an existing foothold trick Defender into writing a malicious file to a protected location to seize full system control.
incidents.impact: Disclosed in Microsoft's record 206-CVE June Patch Tuesday as the one bug under active attack (added to CISA KEV May 20); the release also included the 'wormable' kernel flaw CVE-2026-45657 (CVSS 9.8) and three publicly disclosed zero-days.

incidents.vector: Two Russia-aligned clusters sent weaponized emails with malicious RAR archives exploiting the patched WinRAR path-traversal flaw CVE-2025-8088 to drop payloads into Windows Startup locations.
incidents.impact: One cluster deployed the GiftedCrook info-stealer to harvest credentials and documents; a second (Gamaredon) delivered HTA-based espionage malware against military innovation centers, formations and law-enforcement targets. Activity remains ongoing.

incidents.vector: Iranian hackers breached the news agency's website, deleted articles and disrupted online broadcasts.
incidents.impact: The Handala group claimed the attack and threatened to dox and harm employees of the independent all-female news outlet.

incidents.vector: An attacker compromised a Tchap account, joined public channels and harvested conversations.
incidents.impact: Scraped data was posted to a hacking forum; officials suspended the account and urged staff to use the app's encrypted chat feature for sensitive topics.

incidents.vector: Customer financial and securities data was stolen through an unnamed third-party service provider.
incidents.impact: Data on some of the division's customers was exfiltrated via the supply-chain compromise.

incidents.victim: Two Hokkaido hospitals (180,000+ patients and staff)
incidents.vector: Two decommissioned hospital hard drives containing personal data were put up for sale on an online auction site.
incidents.impact: The personal information of more than 180,000 patients and employees was exposed through improper disposal of storage media.

incidents.vector: Meta says NSO Group ran a new spear-phishing operation luring select WhatsApp users to click malicious links leading to an external site, in violation of an October 2025 US court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta filed a contempt complaint asking the court to hold NSO accountable and urged US lawmakers to keep NSO on the sanctions list; researchers say the legally cornered vendor has grown more reckless.

incidents.victim: Microsoft (Azure GitHub repositories) and downstream CI/CD users
incidents.vector: A variant of the Shai-Hulud worm ('Miasma', tied to TeamPCP) compromised 73 Microsoft GitHub repos, planting config files for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code that auto-execute a 4.6MB credential-stealing payload when a repo is opened in an AI coding tool.
incidents.impact: 73 repos — including Azure/functions-action — were taken offline, breaking CI/CD pipelines globally; anyone who cloned an affected repo after June 2 and opened it in the targeted tools is urged to assume compromise and rotate all credentials.

incidents.victim: US law, professional and financial-services firms
incidents.vector: The UNC3753 cluster (aka 'Luna Moth'/Silent Ransom Group) uses voice phishing and IT-helpdesk impersonation to push victims into screen-sharing and RMM tools, then exfiltrates sensitive files; in some cases operatives entered offices in person posing as IT technicians to copy data to USB.
incidents.impact: Dozens of US firms hit from January–May 2026, with full theft-to-extortion cycles often inside a single business day; in one case 16GB was stolen. The FBI has warned US law firms specifically about the in-person variant.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; the flaw was reportedly exploited since at least April.
incidents.impact: ServiceNow quietly patched the platform and notified affected customers, mainly those on its Australia release.

incidents.vector: An Elasticsearch database was left exposed on the internet without authentication for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Personal details of almost 19 million customers — tied to WeChat accounts and including phone numbers and full names — were exposed before the server was secured.

incidents.vector: A former IBM VP of threat intelligence alleges in a whistleblower lawsuit that both companies' systems were repeatedly breached over years by attackers linked to foreign governments.
incidents.impact: The complaint claims IBM and AT&T concealed the intrusions from the US government and made false security assurances to win and keep federal contracts.

incidents.victim: Obama White House & US Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI support assistant into adding an attacker email to target accounts during the password-reset flow (using a VPN IP near the target's hometown), enabling account takeover.
incidents.impact: The Obama White House and Chief Master Sergeant of the Space Force Instagram accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian content; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed Oxford's CareerConnect careers portal at the end of May and stole stored data.
incidents.impact: Data of alumni, research staff and employers using the platform for internships and recruitment was exfiltrated.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed the malicious Nx Console VS Code extension — compromised in the TanStack supply-chain attack — which exfiltrated internal source code.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 internal GitHub repositories were stolen and offered for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens. Grafana linked a separate breach to the same TanStack incident.

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and a large trove of other agency secrets to a public GitHub account.
incidents.impact: The leak exposed sensitive cloud credentials for CISA's server infrastructure; the agency is still working to invalidate the keys, and lawmakers in both houses of Congress are demanding answers.
